summary: The contract identifies a genuine directly comparable one-unit upper-bound target under matching conventions. Primary records support the separation from the ground-set theorem, the versioned comparison with upper 68, and the ordinary imported-theorem framing. The bounded novelty language is appropriate. A minor attribution revision is needed for the classical lower construction and triple extremum. This round does not certify the complete new proof or exhaustive originality.
required_revisions: In Sections 2 and 3, credit the classical provenance of the 27-member construction and resulting lower 54 to Abbott and Hanson, and the exact triple extremum M(3,3)=20 to Abbott and Gardner. Add bibliographic references or explicitly attribute these through reference [1]; distinguish the classical construction from the new intersecting upper bound in [1].

findings.statement: The manuscript names the recent source for the 27-member equality construction and uses the triple bound 20, but omits their classical provenance. Reference [1] explicitly credits Abbott and Hanson for its construction (6.14), and Abbott and Gardner for (6.1).
findings.disposition: Add the requested historical attribution without changing the imported theorem contracts. Evidence is [1], Section 6.1, paragraph after (6.14), Table 1, and references [2] and [4].

findings.statement: The current novelty claim is bounded to the strongest comparable primary bound located by the recorded search; it does not claim exhaustive priority or a solution of the all-rank conjecture.
findings.disposition: Retain these qualifications in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. Theorem 2 also appropriately declines a separately exhaustive novelty claim.

findings.statement: The H27 source is a computer-assisted preprint whose original exhaustive computation has not been replayed locally; Jin is checked through an explicitly identified scholarly restatement.
findings.disposition: The manuscript discloses these boundaries adequately. Ordinary theorem import is a legitimate framing; the source status does not establish local independent certification.

checks.scope: Frozen round identity and literal theorem
checks.method: Computed SHA-256 of manuscript bytes and of sorted compact UTF-8 snapshot JSON; read contract and roster.
checks.observation: Both hashes match the supplied commitments. Section 1 defines maximum family size, distinct members, exact rank four and empty-core sunflowers; exclusion of 68 therefore means M(4,3)<=67.

checks.scope: Direct rank-four comparison and source version
checks.method: Opened the primary aiXiv abstract record and compared it with Sections 1-2 and the frozen foundation ledger.
checks.observation: [aiXiv v1 record](https://aixiv.online/abs/2610.01292), abstract and submission history, reports exclusion of 69, upper 68, the same simplicity/rank/empty-core conventions, 9 October 2026 v1, and the cited companion commit. It explicitly does not exclude 68.

checks.method: Opened the primary versioned full text and inspected definitions, Proposition 6.7, Proposition 6.8 and Theorem 6.9.
checks.observation: [Axante et al. v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06175v1), Sections 2.1 and 6.3-6.5, agrees with the manuscript conventions and states the intersecting upper 27 and unrestricted interval 54 to 83. Its arbitrary-support reduction precedes exhaustive search.

checks.scope: Historical attribution of imported finite facts
checks.method: Compared manuscript Sections 2-3 and references against the primary paper attribution around equations (6.1) and (6.14).
checks.observation: [Axante et al. v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06175v1) identifies Abbott-Gardner (1969) for the triple extremum and Abbott-Hanson, On finite Delta-systems (1974), for the classical construction. These origins are missing from the reviewed manuscript bibliography and prose.

checks.method: Opened the primary Bucić-He-Lee versioned abstract and compared its quantifiers with Theorem 1.
checks.observation: [Bucić-He-Lee v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26686v1), abstract, treats families of subsets of an n-element ground set and exponential growth in n for every k>=3. It is not the same parameter statement as the arbitrary-support rank-four upper 67. The manuscript makes this distinction explicitly.

checks.scope: Jin theorem contract in the cited restatement
checks.method: Opened Nikiforov PDF and inspected Theorem A on PDF page 2.
checks.observation: [Nikiforov v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.2070v1), Theorem A, has 1<=k<=9, triangle-freeness and strict minimum degree greater than (k+1)n/(3k+2), concluding a homomorphism to A_k. This matches Section 2; no assumed surjectivity is present.

checks.scope: Negative literature-search claim and reported formalization status
checks.method: Read FRONTIER_REFRESH.md, general.md and their named general-search-log.json; compared limitations with manuscript Section 2.
checks.observation: The logs distinguish indexed discovery from exhaustive archive enumeration and record inaccessible pinned formalization files. The manuscript preserves these limitations and does not assert a local build or transitive axiom audit of the external Lean project. I did not rerun the entire search.
